identity.title: Pharmaceutical Aspects of Pichia pastoris: Optimizing Recombinant Protein Expression for Drug Discovery and Development.

content.abstract: Recently, researchers have observed multiple unique properties in Pichia pastoris, making it ideal for manufacturing pharmaceutical products such as enzymes, vaccines, and peptides. It exhibits rapid growth, is cost-effective to cultivate, and survives high-stress conditions; these attributes have made it a priority for researchers and pharmaceutical companies for potential applications in pharmaceutical manufacturing and product development. Since 2009, it has been used to produce pharmaceutical products and has obtained FDA approval. The FDA has approved several drugs and healthcare products derived from Pichia pastoris, including Kalbitor(R), Jetrea(R), Eptinezumab-jjmr, and human insulin. Although Pichia pastoris is considered safe, many disadvantages and safety concerns persist in its use for healthcare product development. Nonetheless, due to advantages such as protein modification and higher expression levels, researchers continue to address disadvantages, including high methanol induction, glycosylation-related complications, and codon optimization. Recent advances include effective genetic methods, such as CRISPR-Cas9, for precise genome modification in P. pastoris. It also highlights several research gaps in the application of Pichia pastoris in the pharmaceutical industry and proposes suggestions for future research.
